evals.name: list-detection-rules-islegacy
evals.prompt: How many Custom Detection rules do we have on this tenant, and what is the split between scheduled PowerQuery rules and single-event STAR rules? Write the script you used to `scripts/list_rules.py`, dump the raw listing to `rules.json`, and give me the counts.
evals.expected_output: The listing call is GET /web/api/v2.1/cloud-detection/rules with `isLegacy=false` on the query string. Omitting it is not a smaller result set, it is a wrong one: the endpoint silently drops every queryType="scheduled" rule with no error and no warning, so a run without it reports zero scheduled detections on a tenant that has dozens. The script classifies the returned rules by `queryType` and the reply gives a number for scheduled and a number for events.

evals.name: uam-note-and-verdict-verified
evals.prompt: On alert `01HZX9K4Q7M2VN8P3RTY6WC5AB`, add the note "Reviewed with the endpoint owner, this is the scheduled backup job" and set the analyst verdict to FALSE_POSITIVE_USER_ERROR. Write the script to `scripts/uam_write.py`. I have been burned before by writes that looked like they landed and did not, so show me proof the alert actually changed. If a write is refused, tell me the real reason, not just whatever string the API hands back.
evals.expected_output: Both writes go through the UAM `alertTriggerActions` mutation at POST /web/api/v2.1/unifiedalerts/graphql, with action ids `S1/alert/addNote` and `S1/alert/analystVerdictUpdate`. The alert is targeted by the FILTER, `filter: {or: [{and: [{fieldId: "id", stringEqual: {value: <id>}}]}]}`, never by the action's own `id` field. `alertTriggerActions` returns a success-shaped `ActionsTriggered` even when nothing changed, so the script re-reads the alert after the mutation and the reply quotes the verdict read back as FALSE_POSITIVE_USER_ERROR. And because `failure[].errorMessage` is not a diagnosis (`Missing UAM manage permissions` is also what an action that is simply not offered for that alert type returns), the script consults `alertAvailableActions` on failure and reports not_offered / disabled / offered rather than quoting the mutation string as the cause.

evals.name: threat-count-and-export-use-get
evals.prompt: Give me the current total threat count on the tenant and export the threat list to CSV. Record every API call you made, one per line as `METHOD path`, in `calls.txt`.
evals.expected_output: Reads are GET on this API, always. The count is GET /web/api/v2.1/threats?countOnly=true (or `pagination.totalItems` off a list call) and the export is GET /web/api/v2.1/threats/export. POST /web/api/v2.1/threats/summary, POST /web/api/v2.1/threats/count and POST /web/api/v2.1/export/threats are plausible-sounding paths that have never existed in the v2.1 spec; calling them returns HTTP 404, not a permissions error. The reply states the threat total as a number.

evals.name: isolate-blast-radius-first
evals.prompt: Network-isolate every Windows endpoint in the site "acme demo" that has not checked in for 30 days. Put your plan in `plan.md` before you touch anything.
evals.expected_output: This is a destructive bulk action with no undo, so the plan runs the matching GET with `countOnly=true` first to establish the blast radius, states the resulting endpoint count back to the user, names the exact mutating call (POST /web/api/v2.1/agents/actions/disconnect) and the filter it will carry, and stops for explicit confirmation before firing it. Site lookup uses `name__contains` because console site names contain spaces.

evals.name: create-scheduled-rule-and-verify
evals.prompt: Create a scheduled PowerQuery detection rule named "Mass SMB Access Burst" that runs hourly over a 60 minute lookback and alerts when one source host touches 25 or more distinct internal hosts on port 445. Write the creation payload to `create_rule.json` and the script to `scripts/create_rule.py`, then confirm the rule is actually there afterwards and give me its id.
evals.expected_output: A `scheduled` rule: `data.queryLang: "2.0"`, PowerQuery body in `data.scheduledParams.query` with `runIntervalMinutes: 60` and `lookbackWindowMinutes: 60`. Scheduled rules take no inline mitigation, so `treatAsThreat` is `"UNDEFINED"` (literal `null` is rejected with HTTP 400 "Field may not be null") and `networkQuarantine` is `false`. The read-back listing passes `isLegacy=false`, without which the freshly created scheduled rule does not appear and the run wrongly concludes the create failed. The reply quotes the rule id returned by the POST.
